correctness.rationale: Complete rank-one one-variable types over two named strict orders are equivalent to the four quadrant-existence masks. Every nonendpoint has one occupied left and right quadrant, giving nine candidates; two mixed monotone-separator masks 6 and 9 cannot coexist, so at most eight nonendpoint masks plus two endpoints. The explicit ten-point witness realizes 10. The C++17 verifier exhaustively visits \(10!=3,628,800\) distinct permutations, counts 164 maximizers of each of two spectral masks, and partitions the 328 maximizers into 46 orbits under all eight order reversals/interchanges. An independently implemented Python prefix/suffix-extrema enumeration confirms the 164+164 counts. This finite enumeration proves only the finite census, never the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: A natural finite model-theoretic capacity question asks how many pointed rank-one logical types can coexist inside one permutation model. Naively 16 quadrant occupancies are logically possible pointwise, but endpoint scarcity and the incompatibility of two order-separator configurations limit simultaneous diversity to 10; a natural sharp ten-point witness exists. The exact first extremal stratum (328 models, two possible spectra and 46 symmetry orbits) is a complete, reproducible finite benchmark with a structural reason for the obstruction, not a minor parameter adjustment or unmotivated slice. It does not claim a broader higher-rank theorem.
